spec.answerVisibility: Literal original givens only; no derived dimension or answer added.

answer.worked:
Each equal-side triangle has its apex on the perpendicular bisector of the common base. The horizontal apex separation is therefore the difference of their perpendicular heights.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\tfrac12(16)(h_{\rm outer}-h_{\rm inner})\\A&=\tfrac12(16)(10)=80\\A&=80\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: The triangle has perpendicular height $12\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Actual user-approved clarification:12cm explicitly labels the perpendicular triangle height from apex to diameter line. Semicircle radius8cm and all original outline/radius/centre structures retained. Right-angle foot marks the approved height; no sloping side length is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Original radius8cm and actual user-approved perpendicular height12cm; no computed area.

answer.worked:
The semicircle has radius $8\text{ cm}$, so its area is $\frac12\pi(8)^2=32\pi\text{ cm}^2$. The triangle has base $16\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $12\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac12\times16\times12+32\pi\\&=(96+32\pi)\text{ cm}^2\\&\approx196.53\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$
